clue.text: Old coach station, one adopted by hunt

parts.note: a post is a station or position someone is assigned to

indicators.note: something adopted is taken into a family, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: to hunt is to chase
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A historic coaching inn where a traveller was once taken in by a hunting party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old coach station' reads naturally as one phrase, a coaching inn, but the definition stops at 'coach' and 'station' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-chaise was a hired horse-drawn carriage of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Structure on sailing ship going up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same whether you go upward or downward

parts.note: a four-letter word that is the same read in either direction

explanation.surface: Something on an old sailing ship that rises and falls with the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The poop is the raised deck at the stern; the word reads the same both ways, which in a down light means up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: The poop deck is a raised superstructure at the stern of a traditional sailing vessel.

clue.text: Winter sport aid's existence briefly revealed in burlesque

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by dropping its final letter
something revealed in a thing is shown sitting inside it

parts.note: a skit is a comic parody, a burlesque
life, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A claim that a piece of winter sports kit made an appearance in a comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: LIF(E) goes into SKIT between the I and the T; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift carries skiers uphill, an essential aid for the winter sport.

clue.text: Family fortune divided by the Spanish on the quiet

parts.note: a clan is an extended family

indicators.note: a word divided by another is split apart with that other placed in the gap

parts.note: fortune or fate
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A family's money being shared out with Spanish relatives in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided by' suggests arithmetic, but here one word is split open to take in another.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something clandestinely means doing it secretly, out of sight.

clue.text: Bird enclosure principally approached by public transport

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, at the head, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter
via means by way of
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Directions to a bird house that is best reached by bus or train.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large cage or building in which birds are kept.

clue.text: Like a nun, possibly, knowing about revised rites

indicators.note: something revised is reworked, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: knowing in the sense of cunning, artful
the letters of rites rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun who knows all about the changes to church ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged rites sit inside SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is called Sister, so behaviour befitting her might be sisterly; the 'possibly' flags the pun.

clue.text: Elegant style originally conceived here in ancient Rome

indicators.note: originally points to the very beginning, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: first letter
hic is Latin for 'here'

explanation.surface: A claim that fashionable style was first dreamt up in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Ancient Rome spoke Latin, in which hic means here.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic as a noun is stylishness and elegance, especially in dress.

clue.text: Greek woman engaged by high-ranking diplomat

indicators.note: someone engaged by another is taken on, held within their service

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Greek woman hired by a senior ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek woman' reads as one unit, but only 'Greek' defines; woman is the name inside HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a Greek, from Hellas, the Greeks' own name for their country.

clue.text: Vehicle in this way met by chap's brother?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
thus means in this manner
a man's name; the 's is part of the surface

explanation.surface: A sibling arriving in a car to meet someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Brother here is a member of a religious order, not a sibling; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Carthusian is a monk of the order founded by St Bruno, and monks are addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Old Baltic port initially misrepresented in Japanese art

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Riga is the capital and port of Latvia

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letters of the next words count

parts.note: first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A Latvian port wrongly portrayed in a Japanese artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' looks like an anagram signal, but it only supplies its first letter, with that of 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Small snake biting large supplier of 24 needs

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: biting means having teeth in something, so one piece is clamped inside the other

parts.note: the adder is Britain's venomous snake
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A little snake sinking its fangs into something big.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is EQUESTRIAN, and a rider needs a saddle; L goes inside ADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler makes and sells saddles and harness, the gear a horse rider requires.

clue.text: Embarrassing woman's noted performance in golf

parts.note: Di's, the possessive of the name Di
a musical performance, one played in notes
taken as written
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman's well-known golfing display that left everyone red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' suggests famous, but it means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disconcerting unsettles or embarrasses, throwing a person off balance.

clue.text: Uncultivated region where angry sea eagles start to squabble

parts.note: wild with anger
the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: the start of the next word is its opening letter only

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A wild place where furious sea eagles begin fighting among themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is wild land left untouched by farming or building.

clue.text: Old character in theatre played Macbeth at last

indicators.note: at last means at the end, so each word yields only its final letter

parts.note: final letters of the three words

explanation.surface: An old actor who finally got to play Macbeth on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' sounds like a veteran actor; it is a letter of an old alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Edh, or eth, is a letter of the Old English alphabet, written ð.

clue.text: Like some universities, say, breaking random local tie

indicators.note: random means in no fixed order, so these letters are jumbled
one word breaking another bursts into its middle

parts.note: the letters of local tie rearranged
eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Some university types interrupting a stray piece of neckwear from round here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual cue for an example abbreviation, here the one meaning 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Collegiate universities, such as Oxford and Cambridge, are made up of separate colleges.

clue.text: Dozy bachelor finally lost in river

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: last letter
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A sleepy single man who has finally disappeared into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally lost' sounds like the bachelor vanishing; it just gives the last letter of 'lost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, dim, which is a sense of dozy in British usage.

clue.text: Flowers bitterns possibly observed around lake?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the birds enclose the single letter

parts.note: the bittern is famous for its booming call, so it is a boomer
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers spotting flowers and bitterns around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The bittern, a marsh bird, makes a deep booming call; 'possibly' allows that other things boom too.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers are things that bloom, so they can whimsically be called bloomers.

clue.text: French loaf ugly old woman consumed, as some would say

indicators.note: this points to how certain speakers pronounce the words, so their sound matters

parts.note: a bag is an ugly old woman; ate means consumed

explanation.surface: An unpleasant old woman wolfing down a French loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as some would say' admits the match depends on accent: ATE spoken as 'et'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is the long thin loaf typical of French bakeries.

clue.text: Like tears of US city crook dropping in

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of something, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a crook is a criminal
the word to be removed

explanation.surface: A tearful moment in an American city when a crook drops in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' suggests a visit; it means removing IN from CRIMINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrimal means relating to tears, as in the lacrimal glands that produce them.

clue.text: Sails south to solicit votes

parts.note: canvas is the cloth sails are made of, and stands for them
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A boat heading south while campaigning for votes.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to go round seeking people's support in an election.

clue.text: Flowering shrub a couple of accountants found around island

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: found around means placed surrounding, so the letters wrap the next piece

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant, twice
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Two accountants stumbling on a flowering bush on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: CA is a chartered accountant; I goes inside the pair after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is a genus of shrubs and trees, such as wattle, bearing clusters of yellow flowers.

clue.text: Seaside device for drying hops, perhaps, in California

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A beachside contraption for drying hops found in California.
explanation.walkthrough: Oast houses, with their cone-shaped roofs, are a feature of Kent's hop country in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal means at or near the coast, the seaside.

clue.text: Line on map represents round watering hole

parts.note: to represent something is to be it
O is round in shape
a watering hole is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A map symbol marking a circular drinking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Trap bringing about mother's ruin?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a snare for catching animals; the letters inside 'bringing' are a coincidence
second meaning: old slang for a certain spirit

explanation.surface: A snare that brings about a mother's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is a British nickname for gin, from its eighteenth-century reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for animals, and also the juniper-flavoured spirit nicknamed mother's ruin.

clue.text: Rider's hesitation about expedition in surrounding area

indicators.note: about means around, so the hesitation wraps the expedition

parts.note: er, the sound of hesitating
a quest is an expedition in search of something

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so the word in wraps the area

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A horse rider dithering over a trip in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue holds two separate wrappings side by side, each with its own signal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrian as an adjective means relating to horse riding, so it can stand for the possessive 'rider's'.

clue.text: Unite under pressure, perhaps, getting married outside Lima

indicators.note: outside means on the outer side, so the marriage word wraps the letter

parts.note: to wed is to get married
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A couple pressured into marrying somewhere outside the capital of Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the Peruvian city but is just a phonetic-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To weld is to join metal pieces, often with heat or pressure, into one.

clue.text: One who breaks down in the lab? A record producer, we hear

definitions.text: One who breaks down in the lab?

indicators.note: we hear points to the spoken form, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: an annalist writes annals, historical records

explanation.surface: A lab worker suffering a breakdown, who also happens to produce records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks down' suggests a collapse, but means separates a substance into its parts; 'record producer' suggests music, not a chronicler.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical analyst separates substances into their components to identify them.

clue.text: Edgy UK native extremely tense crossing lake

parts.note: a Briton

indicators.note: letters crossing another piece span across it, holding it in the middle
extremely refers to the extremes, the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: first and last letters
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A nervous Briton, very tense, making his way across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely tense' sounds like very anxious; it keeps just the ends of 'tense'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brittle can describe a nervy, touchy manner, close to being on edge.

clue.text: She features in novel, say? Yes and film

definitions.text: She features in novel, say? Yes and film

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear within it, so the name sits inside the next words

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A quiz question confirming that a female character appears in both a book and its screen version.
explanation.walkthrough: Elsa the lioness is the star of Joy Adamson's book Born Free and of the film made from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes Elsa, the lioness heroine of Born Free in print and on screen.

clue.text: Unkempt educationist left in threadbare clothing

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the clothing word

parts.note: ragged clothes are worn and tattered
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A scruffy teacher left standing in worn-out clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: An educationist here is anyone holding a teaching degree, abbreviated from Bachelor of Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled means untidy and dishevelled, as if wet and muddied.
